title: HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 streaming negotiation shim with gap-aware resume and function-call mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an interoperability shim that allows clients on older HTTP/1.1 runtimes (expecting SSE/JSONL) to connect to servers that prefer HTTP/2 event streams or server-push, while preserving stream continuity, ordered function-call boundaries, and resume behavior across reconnects and protocol downgrades. This ticket covers protocol negotiation, chunk/fragment identity mapping across protocol transitions, gap detection and heal strategy, and UX for client-side reconnect/backoff behavior. The shim must be stateless where possible and provide a compact resume token compatible with existing resume/token formats used by the Console and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Client connects using Negotiation: server advertises 'stream-profiles' header listing supported stream encodings (http2-push,eventstream-jsonl,chunked-jsonl)
When a server prefers HTTP/2 push but the client only supports HTTP/1.1, the shim downgrades the stream to chunked JSONL with deterministic fragment IDs preserved
Resume token format includes stream-id, fragment-offset, and a 64-bit fragment-hash; the server verifies token and accepts resume at exactly the correct byte-offset or returns 410 if incompatible
Function-call frames are atomic across protocol switches: a function-call must not be split across a downgrade boundary without a reassembly marker
Reconnect backoff adheres to progressive jitter rules and preserves an idempotency key when replaying requests
Performance overhead of the shim in steady state on a p99 HTTP2->HTTP1 downgrade path is <5% CPU compared to native HTTP/2 streaming path under our benchmark (locally measured)
Automated integration tests cover: HTTP/2 push -> chunked JSONL downgrade, resume token acceptance/rejection, function-call boundary preservation, and intentional fragment-loss recovery
design_notes: We will use a thin on-box proxy layer implemented in Rust in the serving tier that can translate HTTP/2 DATA frames with pseudo-headers into chunked JSONL lines. Each outgoing logical chunk will be annotated with a deterministic Fragment-ID computed as blake3(stream-id || sequence-number || first-8-bytes-of-payload). Resume token will be base64(stream-id || seq || byte-offset || fragment-hash) to keep it compact. For clients that call functions/tools mid-stream, we inject an explicit 'call_boundary' sentinel that is preserved when downgrading. See Confluence doc linked below for wire diagrams and binary examples.
implementation_plan: Prototype shim module and unit tests (Rust) - branch streaming/compat/shim-proto
Add headers: Server advertises 'X-Stream-Profiles' and accepts 'X-Stream-Preference' from client
Implement deterministic Fragment-ID generator and compact resume token encoder/decoder
Integrate function-call boundary sentinel and ensure atomic emission on downgrade
Benchmark CPU and latency delta under synthetic traffic (tokenized prompts with tool-calls)
Create integration tests in infra/streaming-integration that run both HTTP/2 native clients and HTTP/1.1 legacy clients against the shim
testing_plan: Unit tests for token encode/decode edge cases (truncated tokens, wrong hash)
Fuzz resume token acceptance to ensure no unsafe seeks
Integration test where server intentionally drops fragments 3 and 4; client reconnects with resume token and validates missing fragments are requested or server returns context 410
Chaos test: simultaneous leads (1000 clients) where 30% are downgraded; verify p99 latency SLA holds
End-to-end test validating function-call reassembly: ensure tool invocation occurs exactly once after reconnect
rollout_plan: Deploy shim behind a feature flag on staging, expose negotiation headers to SDK beta clients. Gradual rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 100% of edge traffic over two weeks. Monitor reconnection rates, resume token rejection rate, and function-call duplication metrics. If resume_token_reject_rate > 0.1% for >1h, rollback the feature flag.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fragment-hash collision could cause incorrect resume location. Mitigation: use 64-bit blake3 truncated digest plus sequence check and reject tokens if sequence mismatch
Risk: Downgrade adds CPU load. Mitigation: offload heavy hashing to worker pool and tune batching thresholds
Risk: Function-call duplication on replay. Mitigation: attach server-side idempotency keys and dedupe by call id on tool invocation endpoints
notes: Design reviewed with Runtime team 2025-02-20. Runtime suggested reusing existing resume token namespace to simplify Console support. Security reviewed preliminary token format for leak risk — tokens are short-lived (1 hour) and bound to a session key.
